currentContext.expansion: Smruthi Organics describes FY 2025-26 as a year of regulatory rather than physical expansion. The Company received EDQM (European Directorate for the Quality of Medicines & HealthCare) approval during the year, which management calls a turning point in its international growth trajectory and which qualifies its APIs for European Union markets and the many countries that accept EDQM certification as their benchmark. It is expanding its Drug Master File portfolio across Europe, Brazil and Korea, and is awaiting a regulatory inspection by ANVISA, Brazil, which management views as the route into South America. On the footprint side, the Company runs R&D centres at Solapur and Hyderabad, both of which received capital and recurring R&D spend during the year per Annexure II to the Directors' Report. Expansion into new activity is commercial rather than asset-led: the Company has begun onboarding customers in Contract Research and Manufacturing Services (CRAMS) and is growing supply of late-stage intermediates to large global API manufacturers. In the opposite direction, the Finished Dosage Formulations (FDF) division is being discontinued as non-core, with wind-down to be completed during the current year. Management states explicitly that capital expenditure will remain moderate and routine unless significant new capacity requirements emerge, as the infrastructure investments of prior years have established a strong foundation. Energy-efficiency investments completed during the year (Annexure II, sourced from the strategy/profile bundles which carried the same annexure) include Multiple Effect Evaporator plant optimisation, approximately 148 LED lighting units, twelve solar-powered outdoor lighting units, variable frequency drives on compressed-air and HVAC systems, cooling-tower optimisation, enhanced HVAC controls and advanced condenser technology for solvent recovery. No new plant, line, capacity addition or commissioning timeline is disclosed anywhere in the routed text.
